items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7861

SPONSOR: MAY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to direct the department of agriculture and markets, in cooper-
ation with the New York state energy research and development authority,
to develop and produce guidance and educational materials on the use of
agrivoltaics in farming

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to promote the benefits to farmers of the
co-location of solar power systems on active farmland for crop
production, reduced energy costs, and climate resilience.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

The department of agriculture and markets, in cooperation with the New
York state energy research and development authority, is directed to
develop guidance and educational materials on the use of agrivoltaics in
farming. For purposes of the bill, the term agrivoltaics is defined as
the co-location of photovoltaic panels and agriculture and/or animal
grazing, for the simultaneous production of electricity and crops on the
same land.

The educational materials produced would include the potential for
reduced electricity costs, reduced water use, enhanced marketing and
potential for extended growing seasons for shade-resistant crops. The
guidance should also include standards for such things as pollinator
friendly practices.

The department is directed to provide a booth at the next New York state
fair for educating the public on the use of agrivoltaics in farming.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Agrivoltaics consists of integrating photo-voltaic modules above crops
in order to enhance climate resilience and allow sustainable food and
energy production on one single piece of land. While in the past it was
a question of either food or solar energy production on farmland, agri-
voltaics can combine both successfully as well as achieving greater
efficiencies on both activities. By working together on the same land,
farmers and energy developers can realize benefits for both endeavors
while preserving the agricultural character of the state's rural commu-
nities.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill
  
FISCAL  IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 27 Chapter 629
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 7861-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  direct  the  department of agriculture and markets, in
        cooperation with the New York state energy research and develop-
        ment authority, to develop and produce guidance and  educational
        materials on the use of agrivoltaics in farming"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  require  the  Department of Agriculture and Markets
(AGM) and the New York State Energy Research and  Development  Authority
(NYSERDA)  to  promote the collocation of solar energy systems on active
farmland, also known as agrivoltaics, through guidance  and  educational
materials.  Agrivoltaics  is  the collocation of renewable energy gener-
ation and agriculture cultivation such as crops, livestock, or  pollina-
tors.
 
  I  fully  support this legislation, as it will promote climate resili-
ence and reduce energy costs for farmers.
 
  However, the  legislation  requires  a  technical  and  administrative
change  to allow AGM and NYSERDA one year to develop guidance and educa-
tional materials on agrivoltaics. I have secured an agreement  with  the
Legislature to make this necessary change.
 
  On the basis of this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Directs the department of agriculture and markets, in cooperation with NYSERDA and institutions of higher education, to develop and produce guidance and educational materials for farmers on the use of agrivoltaics in farming; requires the department of agriculture and markets to provide a booth at the state fair for the purpose of educating the general public on the use of agrivoltaics in farming.
